text:
alex-recruiter: Quick question re: candidate in Toronto (Canadian citizen) — we're prepared to hire as Software Engineer (US remote for East Coast) but they currently can work in US on TN. We plan to file H-1B cap-subject for CY2026. Can they start remote-from-Canada and then move to US once H-1B is approved? Start date target is 2026-10-01.

maya-peopleops: Short answer: yes they can work remotely from Canada before H-1B starts, but a few operational/legal notes. If they will be employed by Redwood US entity and working from Canada, we need to coordinate cross-border payroll/tax and benefits. Did they request to be paid in CAD or USD?

alex-recruiter: Candidate prefers to remain paid in USD if possible. Wants to move to US once H-1B effective date is known.

julia-payroll: Paying a US payroll employee while resident in Canada creates withholding and reporting obligations in Canada (and potentially a separate Canadian payroll or contractor set-up). We need to know expected duration remote-in-Canada and whether they'll be full-time or 1099. Our standard is: if employed by Redwood US and physically working in Canada > short-term business travel, we need to engage HR Ops + local payroll vendor. That takes ~2-3 weeks to stand up.

leo-legal: A couple of immigration points: TN -> H-1B cap-subject is fine, but H-1B start date (if selected) would typically be 2027-10-01 for cap filings submitted in 2026? Wait — confirm which filing cycle you mean. Also note: if they enter US on TN pre-H-1B and are later approved for H-1B, change of status vs consular processing will affect travel options. We should ask candidate about previous entries.

alex-recruiter: We're targeting the 2026 H-1B cap registration (lottery) this spring — if selected and approved, earliest COS would be 2026-10-01 (fiscal year 2027). They plan to stay in Canada until approval and come to US only after COS is active.

leo-legal: OK that aligns. If they remain remote-from-Canada until COS becomes active, less immigration complexity. If they instead try to work in the US on TN and then switch to H-1B COS, they must be careful about travel after approval (travel can void COS if they leave before final approval depending on route). We'll provide detailed guidance once we see whether it's a COS or consular stamp route.

maya-peopleops: Benefits note: we can enroll them in US benefits effective on their US start date. If they're remote in Canada pre-start, they can be ineligible for US medical until US residency begins. We can offer a temporary stipend for private coverage while in Canada if needed. Please confirm budget for bridging health.

julia-payroll: For payroll action items:
- confirm employment country (US entity) and pay currency
- open vendor request if cross-border payroll required
- estimate first US payroll date (after relocation)
If they prefer USD while in Canada, we still need an off-cycle vendor/immigration payroll vendor to handle Canadian tax forms. This requires GL codes and manager approval.

visa-bot: Docs checklist (please upload to secure intake): passport, TN approval copy (if applicable), proof of Canadian residence, signed offer, signed H-1B questionnaire, resume, any prior US visa history. Internal link: [secure intake folder].

alex-recruiter: Candidate asked about benefits enrollment before their US start date (e.g., 401k, health). They want to know if they can enroll now and have coverage start on arrival.

maya-peopleops: Yes, we can provisionally enroll them and set effective date to US start. We'll queue benefits invites in Workday now so enrollment window isn't missed. Documentation (proof of US address) needed before active coverage. For 401(k) we can set deferral to start on first US payroll.

leo-legal: Also flag dependent visas: candidate's spouse will remain in Canada initially. If they later apply for H-4, there will be separate consulate steps for H-4 stamping. We'll include guidance in the immigration packet.

julia-payroll: Operationally: ask candidate to fill out tax residency questionnaire and provide Canadian SIN and US SSN (if they have one). If they don't have SSN, we can onboard without it but payroll will use default withholding until SSN issued.

maya-peopleops: Next steps for recruiter: 1) confirm pay currency and expected remote duration; 2) confirm whether candidate wants bridging health stipend; 3) upload scanned docs to intake. People Ops will then create a cross-border onboarding plan and loop Finance.

alex-recruiter: I'll confirm ASAP. One more: will we cover H-1B filing fees / lawyer costs? Candidate asked who pays premium processing if used.

leo-legal: Company pays standard H-1B petition legal fees and filing fees per policy. Premium processing is approved case-by-case; if we choose premium for speed we cover it for business-critical hires. We'll flag in requisition.

maya-peopleops: Perfect. I'll add an expense code for immigration and cross-border payroll. Thanks everyone :rocket:
